actionDecision: Decide on each action separately. Inspect its authenticated signingSummary against local policy. A short approvalCommand authorizes only that exact digest-bound action, not a standing precommitment. After approval, the adapter preserves exact payload bytes without model transcription. The manifest digest independently pins exact manifest bytes; that manifest pins helper bytes. The host root is separate and verifies session and closing certificate signatures inside the helper, not the asset bootstrap. Refuse any mismatch.
initiator:
Use the configured Clockchain Handshake MCP for this controlled Sepolia test with Harbor Supply, reference NS-1847.

First and immediately, create the one-time Responder invitation before inspecting the preloaded helper assets. The other person will copy it from the MCP result. Do not stop or wait for another prompt; continue the Initiator side.

Exact statement: "Northstar Logistics and Harbor Supply authorize these two independently controlled agents to communicate about shipment reference NS-1847 for 90 seconds."

This is my direct authorization for this agent to complete the bounded handshake autonomously. Create and enforce the exact local policy: this reference and statement, 90 seconds, one fresh ERC-8004 identity per agent, and no external business action. Clockchain's statementDigest is SHA-256 over its canonical full terms object, not the raw statement text; validate the returned terms exactly. Then use only Clockchain MCP and its digest-pinned local helper; inspect the preloaded manifest and helper source. Create one local signing key. Keep role access and private key material local. Sign only exact policy- and session-bound artifacts. For each helper step, run only its exact short approvalCommand as the complete command, with no prefix or suffix. The local harness adapter executes Clockchain's bound arguments directly; never run or reconstruct shellCommand yourself. If approval fails, request the current operation once and approve its new command; stop only if that retry also fails. Every MCP response without a locally verified certificate is nonterminal. On wait or pending, use the bounded retry interval and call the current MCP operation again. Never finish merely because the other role is pending. Continue until the final Clockchain certificate is locally verified. Refuse any policy, identity, signature, session, statement, or digest mismatch.
